title: Add pcb_stackup element for fabricator stackup and material data
description: Adds a new pcb_stackup element to Circuit JSON for carrying resolved physical layer data alongside the board, allowing consumers to access material properties without needing to re-resolve templates or read side files.
body:
## Why

Downstream projects such as `0hmX/am3352-ddr-eye` keep board construction and material properties in a separate `board-construction.json` / `simulation.json`. This PR adds `pcb_stackup`, so Circuit JSON can carry the resolved physical layer data alongside the board. A follow-up in core/props will resolve a fabricator template code, such as JLCPCB `JLC04161H-3313`, and emit the full stackup. Consumers can then use those values without re-resolving the template or reading a side file.

## Schema

- Identifiers: `pcb_stackup_id`, `pcb_board_id`, optional `subcircuit_id`.
- Optional `plated_hole_copper_thickness`: the copper thickness of plated hole and via barrel walls.
- Required `layers`, ordered top to bottom, discriminated by `layer_type`:
  - `soldermask`: `thickness`, `relative_permittivity`
  - `copper`: `layer` (`top`, `inner1`, …, `bottom`), `thickness`, `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m`, `rms_surface_roughness`
  - `dielectric`: `dielectric_type` (`core` | `prepreg`), `material_name`, `thickness`, `relative_permittivity`, `loss_tangent`, `dielectric_properties_frequency_hz`

Lengths accept existing unit strings and are normalized to mm. Physical values must be finite and positive. Roughness and loss tangent may also be zero. When `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m` is omitted, consumers may assume 5.8e7 S/m (annealed copper).

Board thickness and copper weight are not duplicated here: `pcb_board.thickness` already holds the board thickness, and each copper layer's `thickness` holds its resolved value.

## Example

Two-layer board, top to bottom, lengths in mm:

```json
{
  "type": "pcb_stackup",
  "pcb_stackup_id": "pcb_stackup_1",
  "pcb_board_id": "pcb_board_1",
  "plated_hole_copper_thickness": 0.02,
  "layers": [
    { "layer_type": "soldermask", "thickness": 0.01, "relative_permittivity": 3.5 },
    { "layer_type": "copper", "layer": "top", "thickness": 0.035, "electrical_conductivity_s_per_m": 58000000 },
    {
      "layer_type": "dielectric",
      "dielectric_type": "core",
      "material_name": "FR-4",
      "thickness": 1.51,
      "relative_permittivity": 4.3,
      "loss_tangent": 0.02,
      "dielectric_properties_frequency_hz": 1000000000
    },
    { "layer_type": "copper", "layer": "bottom", "thickness": 0.035, "electrical_conductivity_s_per_m": 58000000 },
    { "layer_type": "soldermask", "thickness": 0.01, "relative_permittivity": 3.5 }
  ]
}
```

## Tests

Each file contains a single test:

- `pcb_stackup_jlc_template`: a JLC04161H-3313 fixture parses through `any_circuit_element`, units normalize to mm, and the JSON round trip is stable.
- `pcb_stackup_optional_material_properties`: optional properties are retained, and zero roughness and zero loss tangent are accepted.
- `pcb_stackup_required_fields`, `pcb_stackup_invalid_layers`, `pcb_stackup_invalid_physical_values`: missing fields, unknown layer types or refs, and zero, negative or non-finite values are rejected.

The README has a new `PcbStackup` section, generated with `bun run generate-docs`. Only the stackup section is committed, without unrelated regeneration drift.

## Validation

`bun test` (475 pass), `tsc --noEmit`, `lint:zod`, `check-snake-case`, `build`, `format`: all pass.

title: Reproduce missing pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad footprints
description: Reproduces a bug where the analyzer fails to determine pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad LED and diode footprints due to small coordinate differences, without changing the analyzers functionality.
body:
## Motivation
Imported two-pad LED and diode footprints can contain tiny coordinate differences between pad centers, even when the pads are intended to form a horizontal or vertical row. analyzePcbPin1Location currently treats these footprints as diagonal and returns null.


Core therefore cannot populate pin1_location, leaving downstream assembly and pick-and-place tools unable to verify or adjust the orientation of polarized components. The analyzer should tolerate small import rounding errors while continuing to reject genuinely diagonal footprints.

This PR only reproduces the issue. It does not change the analyzer.

- Uses the exact imported LED and diode pad geometry.
- Generates SVG snapshots directly from those fixtures and the analyzer's current output.
- Uses `test.failing` to document the expected `topside_left` result without treating the current `null` result as correct.

### LED rectangular pads

![LED pad-center skew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-util/feac5eb2e9419d7e1b73e4c803313a4f1fdd210e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-imported-two-pad-pin1-skew-led.snap.svg)

### Diode polygon pads

![Diode pad-center skew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-util/feac5eb2e9419d7e1b73e4c803313a4f1fdd210e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-imported-two-pad-pin1-skew-diode.snap.svg)

- `bun run build`

title: Add polarized option to generic capacitor footprints
description: Adds a polarized option to generic capacitor footprints, allowing for a positive pin marking and specific silkscreen placement without altering existing pad geometry.
body:
Adds `.polarized()` / `_polarized` to generic `cap` footprints. Opting in draws a 0.15 mm silkscreen + beside pin 1, with at least 0.25 mm clearance from copper and body paths. Default/disabled capacitors retain their existing output and pad geometry.

```ts
fp().cap().imperial("0603").polarized().circuitJson()
fp.string("cap0603_polarized").circuitJson()
```

A standalone, smaller alternative to #927: this PR includes only the generic-capacitor flag and its positive-pin-1 marking. It adds no positive/negative pin remapping and changes no radial/electrolytic generators. The cap builder exposes the flag, and the passive definition schema retains it. Contradictory polarized/nonpolarized selections are rejected. Existing origin/rotation and `nosilkscreen` options apply to the new mark.

Validation: **646 tests pass**, production build and changed-file format check pass. New SVG snapshots cover four sizes, opt-in/default/disabled behavior, through-hole holes, transforms, and disabled silkscreen. No new documentation files.

title: Fix nonparallel flex tails in the 3D viewer
description: Fixes rendering issues in the 3D viewer for flex PCB tails with nonparallel bend axes by updating flex-utils and restoring Float32 boundary precision.
body:
Separate encoder and connector tails with nonparallel bend axes fail in the live viewer because it does not supply the board outline needed to resolve independent moving regions. Update bundled flex-utils to 0.0.8 and pass the board-local outline to its existing folding implementation.

Restore Float32 boundary precision when adapting native Three.js meshes so rounded tail edges are classified on the correct moving region instead of remaining flat and forming spikes. This adapter handles Three.js storage precision and mesh transforms; bend-region selection, fold ordering, deformation and CAD transforms remain in flex-utils.

The **Flex PCB → Independent Tails** fixture has a 180° encoder return, a separate 90° connector bend, component markers and stiffeners. Its fractional tail edge reproduces the precision bug. Open [Folded](https://3d-viewer-git-fix-nonparallel-flex-preview-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/flex-pcb-independent-tails--folded) or [Flat](https://3d-viewer-git-fix-nonparallel-flex-preview-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/flex-pcb-independent-tails--flat); right-click **Fold PCBs** to switch states. Regression tests share the fixture and check tail positions, CAD fold/unfold, textures and edge precision.

Apply the repository formatter to the four existing workflow/documentation files reported by CI, including CRLF normalization; workflow behavior is unchanged.

Dependency publication: flex-utils 0.0.8 currently publishes only to GitHub Packages. The public npm registry returns 404, GitHub Packages requires authentication, and jscdn serves tarballs rather than npm registry metadata. Keep the working versioned CDN dependency until flex-utils is published to public npm; replacing it with a bare version now would break clean installs.

Validation: CI passes Format Check, Type Check and Test Node Bundle Load (including the flex regression tests). Repository-wide formatting and the production build also pass locally.

Downloading a hierarchical KiCad project included only the root `.kicad_sch` file. A project with seven child sheets therefore contained just 1 of the 8 required schematic files, leaving the child-sheet references unresolved.

The ZIP includes the root schematic and every child schematic returned by `getOutputFiles()`. The root filename is passed to the converter so child-sheet references and any renamed child files stay consistent.

- Add all converter-generated schematic files directly to the existing ZIP download function.
- Update `@tscircuit/internal-dynamic-import` from `^0.0.15` to `^0.0.20`, which includes the KiCad declarations published after [internal-dynamic-import#42](https://github.com/tscircuit/internal-dynamic-import/pull/42) merged.
- Use `SupportedModuleMap["circuit-json-to-kicad"]` for the loader's KiCad module type.

- Full Bun suite: 417 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed.
- Typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub test, formatting, and typecheck checks passed; Vercel deployment succeeded for `0243fbc`.

description: Pipeline9 can route independent high-density batches through a host-owned SolverRuntime while retaining its existing synchronous solvestep behavior.

Pipeline9 can route independent high-density batches through a host-owned SolverRuntime while retaining its existing synchronous solve/step behavior.

**Merge #3155 first.** It contains only the two Bun version upgrades, pinned to 1.4.3. This branch is based on that prerequisite, with separate commits for the runtime implementation and the complex-board parity test.

The new default-effort dataset18 sample01 test covers 115 connections, 279 obstacles, and 205 routed traces. It runs a fresh synchronous solver and a second solver with **four native Bun workers**, with caches disabled. Strict worker mode rejects unavailable registrations/startup failures; 146 dispatched batches prove the test exercises worker execution.

The checks require:
- Byte-identical complete routed SRJ, with no coordinate rounding, ID normalization, sorting, or tolerance.
- Exact high-density routes before downstream phases can hide differences.
- Identical high-density statistics and phase/pipeline logical iteration counts.
- Successful routing, unchanged source input, and a sufficiently complex board.

Both complete outputs have the same SHA-256 hash, printed in the test log. The checked-in snapshot renders both independently produced boards with the standard relaxed-DRC overlay: **UNTHREADED on the left, 4 THREADS on the right**. Both show zero relaxed-DRC errors.

![Dataset18 sample01: UNTHREADED versus 4 THREADS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/7e27c8e680d68feb239ce2b191d1b15d65f2e7df/tests/features/__snapshots__/pipeline9-srj18-sample01-thread-parity.snap.svg)

Run it with:
```sh
bun test tests/features/pipeline9-srj18-sample01-thread-parity.test.ts --timeout 300000
```

A subprocess fixture bypasses the test suite's SVG preload, which replaces global Worker with Node's adapter, so this test exercises Bun's actual native worker pool. The visual snapshot is separate from the exact data comparisons.

Runtime behavior: registered four-node tasks commit in serial node-pop order; budget-crossing tasks replay the exact remaining prefix. Preloaded-copper dependencies remain serial. Bun/Node factories embed generated worker bundles; default/browser imports remain inline and exclude worker payloads. The host owns runtime disposal, and worker errors reject.

Align package.json once from 0.0.56 to the already published 0.0.67 so pver can select 0.0.68; otherwise the existing ten-tag collision limit [stops publishing before PR creation](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/actions/runs/39170393887). Subsequent bumps use the existing bot workflow. No tags are deleted or republished.

Validation: the actual pver 0.0.43 and create-pull-request v5 branch code were exercised against temporary local Git remotes. Detached checkout produces no PR diff; attached main creates a branch containing 0.0.68, with remote main unchanged. No npm package was published during validation. title: Detect transistor LED misalignment
description: Detects misalignment between a transistor and LED in a rail-to-rail indicator branch, ensuring proper alignment for electrical connections.
body:
Q2 and LED4 in the ESP32 GPS tracker's NETLIGHT indicator are separated with perpendicular connected terminals. `TransistorLedAlignmentSolver` emits `TransistorLedNotAligned` when a typed LED and transistor in a rail-to-rail indicator branch cannot read as a straight facing connection.

Stack: #335 (TSX repro) → this solver PR. Merge the repro first. This stack is independent of the fuse/connector stack.

![Tracker indicator before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/28d4e1f4337530a8fd835abc40a9a542e91266a8/tests/cases/__snapshots__/transistor-led-alignment-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The proof comes from [pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker v1.1.0](https://tscircuit.com/pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker?version=1.1.0#schematic). The corrected TSX rotates Q2 and LED4 into a direct vertical branch, aligns R20 with its transistor terminal, and turns/repositions R16 so its supply terminal is above it. Component values, native symbols and all source electrical records are preserved. Tests also verify visible wire continuity. The complete four-part extract reports **zero findings from all analyzers** after correction.

The committed comparison includes all three original findings, with the original and corrected circuits at equal scale, a divider, red markers and diagnostics below. The original repro and a separate complete corrected-network snapshot are retained. This is an extracted network; the full published board has other findings.

The rule requires native `simple_led`, NPN/PNP `simple_transistor`, and a series `simple_resistor` between opposite declared power/ground rails. It uses typed metadata, connectivity and drawn terminal directions; names, labels, hints and pin numbers do not establish roles. It accepts horizontal or vertical straight connections and compact local bends. Separation must exceed the larger of 2 schematic units or twice the LED's largest dimension, with 0.15 units of lateral tolerance for facing pins. Ambiguous/branched connections, feedback, DNP/DNC, conflicting rails, overlapping bodies, separate scopes and incomplete geometry are skipped.

Existing coverage is demonstrated explicitly: fixing only the R20/Q2 alignment and R16 orientation leaves this LED/transistor finding. The low-side-load solver requires a different chip-load/clamp network, and #282's single-pin extension requires already-horizontal facing terminals. [SIM800 Hardware Design v1.09, page 47, Figure 43](https://simcom.ee/documents/SIM800/SIM800_Hardware%20Design_V1.09.pdf#page=47) illustrates a vertical LED/resistor/transistor branch; its resistor is on the other side of the LED, so the proof retains the published board's own connections rather than copying that circuit.

Validation: **273 tests pass**, plus typecheck, build and formatting. Guards cover renamed names/hints/pin numbers, rail flags, branched/feedback connections, missing/duplicate geometry, DNP/DNC, scope, rotation/reflection, compact bends and alignment tolerance. Both corrected SVGs were rendered and visually inspected. Existing unrelated snapshots, dependencies and timeouts are unchanged.

## What it does
Native tscircuit TSX → routed PCB geometry → FastHenry/FasterCap extraction → `@tscircuit/ibis-to-spice` → ngspice → measured waveforms and eye diagrams. Runtime is plain code, no LLM.

- `src/` — geometry extraction, RLGC matrices, SPICE assembly, native IBIS consumption, eye-diagram metrics, CLI (`pcb-spice-pipeline`), `--repeat` determinism check

- `vendor/` — experimental `@tscircuit/core`/`props` IBIS builds and `ibis-to-spice` tarball
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — Linux CI (not yet exercised; the proof was run on Darwin arm64)

```sh
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline --setup
```

title: Infer pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad footprints
description: Allows the analyzer to infer pin 1 orientation for two-pad footprints with slight coordinate differences, improving compatibility with polarized components.
body:
## Motivation

Imported two-pad LED and diode footprints can contain tiny coordinate differences between pad centers, even when the pads are intended to form a horizontal or vertical row. `analyzePcbPin1Location` currently treats these footprints as diagonal and returns `null`.

Core therefore cannot populate `pin1_location`, leaving downstream assembly and pick-and-place tools unable to verify or adjust the orientation of polarized components. The analyzer should tolerate small import rounding errors while continuing to reject genuinely diagonal footprints.

Repro : https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/pull/221
## Changes

- allow exactly two pads numbered 1 and 2 to have centerline skew up to 1% of their pitch
- retain the stricter existing behavior for multi-pad rows and genuinely diagonal footprints
- convert the merged MuseGrow reproduction into passing regression tests
- update its LED and diode snapshots to show the inferred `topside_left` orientation

title: Add assembly drawing pages, part views, and title blocks
description: Adds assembly.drawing.page, assembly.drawing.partview, and optional assembly.drawing.titleblock schemas for creating assembly drawings with specified dimensions and layout.
body:
Adds `<assembly.drawing.page>`, `<assembly.drawing.partview>`, and optional `<assembly.drawing.titleblock>` schemas. Pages accept standard ISO A0–A4 / ANSI A–E sizes with landscape or portrait orientation, or explicit unit-aware custom dimensions. Named sizes resolve to mm; conflicting dimensions and invalid sheet numbering are rejected.

Part views independently select geometry via `partRef`, with explicit direction, viewport placement using `centerX`/`centerY`, hidden edges and hatched section-plane configuration. `leftOfRef`, `rightOfRef`, `aboveRef`, and `belowRef` describe inferred placement relative to sibling part views. References are nonempty selector strings; opposing references and explicit centers on the same axis conflict. Inferred axes remain undefined in parsed output; unconstrained axes default to zero. The documented layout contract places viewport edges adjacent with no implicit gap. Page-aware reference resolution, cycle detection, and position calculation remain core/exporter follow-up work.

Views automatically fit the selected geometry to their viewport; there is no `scale` prop. These are unreleased components, with no aliases for the previous `target`/`x`/`y` names. No style enum or image/artifact inputs. Enum modes use snake_case; signed-axis TSX direction notation remains unchanged.

Title-block metadata references ISO 7200:2004; sheet references are ISO 5457 and ASME Y14.1, with dimensions cross-checked against Autodesk's sheet-size documentation. Links and interoperability limits are documented. This does not claim full standards-template compliance. Core TSX registration/emission remains follow-up work.

Validation: 724 tests (7 snapshots), typecheck, build, format, and all four required documentation generators pass. Tests cover reference validation and conflicts, inferred axes, center defaults and unit conversion, required partRef, and removal of the old prop names and scale.

Related: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/918 and https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/pull/1.

title: Assembly Explosion Stage and Move Elements
description: Adds props for assembly.explosion.stage and assembly.explosion.move to enable staged disassembly and movement of subassemblies in TSX.
body:
Adds props for `<assembly.explosion.stage>` and `<assembly.explosion.move>` so TSX authors can describe staged disassembly, including moving a subassembly intact before exploding its children at the displaced pose.

Stages accept `name`, optional `nextStageRef` / `prevStageRef`, and preserved children. Moves accept `targetRefs` as a comma-separated string or an array, plus signed, unit-aware `offX` / `offY` / `offZ` normalized to finite millimeters. References are trimmed and parsed to `targetRefs: string[]`. The existing `targetRef` remains a single-target compatibility alias; supply exactly one selector prop. Empty lists and blank members fail validation. Validators and input types are exported individually and through `assemblyProps.explosion`.

The proposal documents document-order fallback, cross-assembly ordering references, accumulated motion, and automatic swept-path collision checks. This PR supplies props and validation; namespaced JSX components, stage scheduling, and collision checking require corresponding core support. No explosion container or run, detach, translate, or collision-check elements are introduced.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 676 passed, 0 failed.
- `tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- `biome format .`: passed.
- All four required documentation generation scripts completed; generated props overview included.

Approval tracking: this PR remains **draft and awaiting API approval**. Related speculative drafts are [core#4631](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4631) for constrained explosion views and PoppyGL renders, and [poppygl#49](https://github.com/tscircuit/poppygl/pull/49) for guide lines. The props/core changes remain draft pending approval; PoppyGL #49 has merged. Core uses pinned previews until the upstream packages are approved and released.

## Multiple targets

Both inputs describe one move, applying the same displacement to all targets:

```tsx
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs="shade, collar" offZ="60mm" />
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs={["shade", "collar"]} offZ="60mm" />
```

Core moves the union of the selected subtrees so duplicate references or parent/child overlaps do not translate a part twice. Parsed references preserve authored order; each distinct selected target can have its own guide. The proposal documents normalization, compatibility, conflicts, and grouped motion.

body:
Adds a core implementation of `assembly.explosion.stage` and `assembly.explosion.move`, including multi-target moves and rendered constrained-assembly examples.

The upstream props and PoppyGL changes are merged. This PR uses their published npm releases.

## Multiple targets

`targetRefs` accepts either a comma-separated string or an array:

```tsx
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs="shade, collar" offZ="60mm" />
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs={["shade", "collar"]} offZ="60mm" />
```

Props trims and normalizes either form to `targetRefs: string[]`. Existing `targetRef` remains a single-target input alias; supply exactly one selector prop. Core resolves and validates every target before evaluating progress, then moves the union of the selected subtrees using one displacement in the stage owner's frame. Duplicate references and overlapping parent/child selections move each part and reference surface only once.

Each distinct selected target gets its own guide, anchored before the instruction moves any target. Model-less container centroids include prior independent movements of their children. All targets share the instruction's progress, and evaluation leaves assembled Circuit JSON and props unchanged.

![Comma-separated and array targets, shared progress, and legacy compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/b16362715bac0d1e544dc2b51eb785e44770bb66/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-target-refs-annotated.snap.png)

## Staged rendering

`getAssemblyExplosion(circuit, { throughStageRef?, stageProgress? })` derives an immutable CAD view after mounting constraints resolve. Stages use a stable topological sort with authored order as fallback; missing/ambiguous references, cycles, duplicate stages, and invalid move targets produce named diagnostics. Parent movement carries descendant CAD and reference-surface centers. Repeated evaluation and backward scrubbing reconstruct the assembled starting state.

Existing examples lift an intact constrained cover, move it aside, and then remove its cap in the displaced subassembly frame. Frame tests cover upright, inverted, and tilted mounts against emitted reference directions, with guide endpoints checked against emitted GLTF translations. Run `bun scripts/render-assembly-explosion.tsx work/assembly-explosion-preview` to export those four PNG/GLB/JSON states.

## Dependencies

- `@tscircuit/props`: `^0.0.707` in dev dependencies and overrides, including the merged stage/move API and `targetRefs` normalization.
- `poppygl`: `0.0.36`, including the merged explosion guide and arrow APIs.
- Updated with main and resolved the package conflict. The existing dependency check is preserved and passes with these registry versions.

The compatibility refresh also removes the unsupported `write: false` option from the existing Bun browser-bundle test; it continues to inspect the returned bundle without an output directory.

## Validation

- 69 assembly regressions and 4 namespaced assembly regressions pass (73 total), using Bun 1.4.0 and the published npm packages.
- Three new tests cover string/array/legacy selectors, shared progress, overlap and duplicate handling in a mounted frame, reference-surface translation without orientation changes, pre-move centroids, and validation of later-stage targets.
- Both new annotated visual snapshots were inspected and pass on comparison.
- Full CI is green on the updated branch: all ten test groups, full typecheck, dependency check, distribution smoke tests, package preview build, and deployment.
- Local package build (including declarations), 73 assembly/namespaced regressions, browser-bundle regression, changed-TypeScript formatting, and feature diff checks pass.

Behavior and approval tracking are documented in `docs/assembly-explosion.md`. This prototype supports mechanical CAD translations and rejects PCB/cable-containing targets. Swept-path collision verification remains unimplemented (`collisionCheckStatus: "not_implemented"`); diagrams do not certify assembly clearance.

body:

```ts
  renderStyle: "outline",
  showHiddenEdges: true,
  section: { axis: "x", offset: 5, keepSide: "less", hatchSpacing: 1 },
})
```

title: Speculative explosion guide lines with optional arrows
description: Adds opt-in explosionLines for assembly diagrams, including optional arrowheads that show the direction a part moves, enhancing the visual representation of exploded views in the rendering engine.
body:
Adds opt-in `explosionLines` for assembly diagrams, including optional arrowheads that show the direction a part moves. Callers supply scene-space polylines and move the geometry themselves; guides respect scene depth without writing to the depth buffer.

Set `arrow: true` on a guide to add a solid open arrowhead at its final authored point. Arrows follow the final nonzero-length segment, remain solid on dashed shafts, and keep a consistent size of up to 10 output pixels under supersampling. Arrows default to off. Off-screen and behind-camera endpoints do not acquire arrowheads at clipping boundaries.

## Lamp example

The lamp shade, collar, and spokes lift **60 mm along +Y**, while the base, hollow blue stem, and bulb stay fixed. Two dashed guides with upward arrowheads join corresponding lower-rim points. Cosmos provides separate **Lift shade**, **Show dashed guides**, and **Show arrows** controls. The assembled and exploded snapshots use the same camera, with deterministic local geometry.

[Interactive lamp preview](https://poppygl-git-speculative-explosion-lines-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixture=%7B%22path%22%3A%22site%2Fexamples%2Fexplosion-lamp.page.tsx%22%7D)

## Rendering

Guide points contribute to automatic camera framing, and segments are clipped to the camera frustum before rasterization. The exported `ExplosionLine` type and README document coordinates, optional arrows, and dashed or solid shafts. Guide and arrow stroke widths use the `lineWidth` option from #52. Omitting guides preserves existing output.

This remains a **speculative draft awaiting API and implementation approval**, supporting the staged assembly proposals in [props#936](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/936) and [core#4631](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4631). The PR package preview workflow allows the core draft to pin this implementation before a release.

title: Add configurable hidden edges and thicker strokes
description: Adds render-wide controls for visible and hidden mesh edges, plus configurable stroke widths, allowing ordinary GLB files to display thick solid visible edges and faint dashed occluded edges without editing node metadata.
body:
Adds render-wide controls for visible and hidden mesh edges, plus configurable stroke widths. An ordinary GLB can now show thick solid visible edges and faint dashed occluded edges without editing its node metadata.

```ts
await renderGLTFToPNGFromGLB(glb, {
  showHiddenEdges: true,
  edgeWidth: 2.5,
  lineWidth: 2,
  hiddenEdgeOpacity: 0.35,
  supersampling: 2,
})
```

- `showEdges` enables visible boundary/crease edges alone. `showHiddenEdges: null` (the default) retains model flags; explicit `false` suppresses them.
- Widths use final output pixels and scale once with supersampling. Ordinary glTF LINES and finite grids use `lineWidth`; extracted mesh edges use `edgeWidth`.
- Wide strokes use antialiased screen-space coverage and frustum clipping in the existing software renderer. Per-pixel depth testing preserves occlusion; source-face depth sampling keeps visible sloping edges solid without a broad depth bias.
- Retains the legacy single-raster-pixel path. Edge overlays do not write geometry depth.
- Includes an interactive lamp example, deterministic lamp/cube visuals, and regressions for width across orientations, fractional alpha, dashes, supersampling, near/eye clipping, extreme endpoints and a close foreground occluder.

The lamp fixture is adapted from core's reference-surface lamp. Its collar, spokes and mounting details are visible through the shade in the right panel.

![Lamp with visible and hidden 2.5 px edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/poppygl/f49ffec8849a9af3d475be5c3a8c493c402de21b/tests/render/__snapshots__/edge-styles-lamp.snap.png)

Open `site/examples/edge-styles-lamp.page.tsx` in Cosmos for shaded/visible/hidden modes and the width slider.

This PR targets main independently of the speculative explosion guide-line PR #49. Edge extraction retains the existing boundary/30-degree crease behavior; it does not add smooth-surface silhouettes. The procedural infinite grid retains its own styling.

description: Fixes the issue where rotating a component with polygon plated holes does not rotate its copper, drill offsets, and soldermask openings, ensuring they align correctly in the 3D viewer.
body:

Oval and pill drills use their existing rotation options; their local offsets are rotated into board coordinates. SMT pads and traces share the existing plated-hole drill calculation. Reuse the existing pill-path helper and build oval cutouts without changing the surrounding compound path's transform.

title: Reuse regional geometry and owned route metadata
description: Optimizes routing by reusing regional geometry and metadata during selective rerips, reducing unnecessary computations and improving performance.
body:
Port-point routing repeated static neighbor checks throughout each owned search, and selective rerips rebuilt intersection geometry even in untouched regions. Reuse both forms of stable state while preserving the selected paths, ordering, routing work, and invariant checks.

<!-- visual-optimization-snapshots -->
### Visual snapshots

PNG previews of the checked SVG regression snapshots, generated from the live reference and optimized test observations.

**Regional metadata reuse.** The port heatmap records 1,447 → 82 hop-ID evaluations over 50 paired steps with identical state and stats.

**Selective region rebuilding.** Ripping route 0 changes only region 0: rebuild one segment instead of five while retaining the same committed copper.

![Visual snapshot: Selective region rebuilding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/__snapshots__/selective-rerip-unchanged-region-cache-visual.preview.png)

The SVGs are regression-tested; the PNGs above are rendered from those exact checked-in SVGs for inline display.
<!-- /visual-optimization-snapshots -->

- Reuse intersection caches when a selective rerip removes no segment from a region. Refresh their scores with the current geometry and cost parameters; continue validating every committed port owner.
- Lazily cache successful section, incidence, hop-ID, assignment, and reservation checks inside the existing opt-in `OWNED_REGIONAL_HOP_FRONTIER` contract. Live closure, best costs, congestion, penalties, and scoring still run for each candidate. Lazy preparation preserves early-goal and exception order.
- Invalidate retained metadata when the heap, closure epoch, route, net, goal, best-cost generation, or neighbor-array identity changes. The existing ownership contract requires fixed ordinary metadata within an epoch; the default and opt-out search paths are unchanged.

The neighbor metadata idea is adapted from [#208](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/208). This patch isolates cache reuse; it excludes that PR's owner-floor, dominance-pruning, and tie-order changes.

Validation with snapshot regression coverage (production unchanged from benchmarked `bee74730028acc3fe72a1132bef3ef89df0238d7`):

- All 152 tests pass with 2,889 assertions; TypeScript and changed-file formatting checks pass.
- Differential tests compare working state, subsequent output and iterations, native closure, queue replacement, best-cost resets, route/net/goal boundaries, neighbor replacement, no-op and selective rerips, shared endpoints, recommits, and loud ownership errors. Existing malformed-incidence, early-goal, and scoring-error cases preserve the exact exception order and messages.
- A work-count replay of the actual current autorouter's SRJ18 sample 6 retains the exact port-output SHA-256 `b6d233e9f40324bacc9393ce4038ec8ec155cc91433b083d49a392546681e860`, every non-timing solve-graph metric, all 2,000,000 inner iterations, and all 5,683,414 frontier expansions.
- In that replay, hop-key evaluations fall from 355,788,254 to 28,854,609 (91.89% fewer), port-reservation checks from 351,821,820 to 28,855,122 (91.80% fewer), and region-reservation checks from 338,725,099 to 15,758,401 (95.35% fewer). The 330,211,264 best-cost checks and 79,581,560 scoring calls remain identical. This omits 972,867,041 repeated static helper calls.

SRJ18 regional port pathing takes 5.97% less time overall and 13.43% less on sample 6 in the combined consumer benchmark. The combined consumer patch is benchmarked in [tscircuit-autorouter #3160](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3160): 107 scenarios on paired Blacksmith ARM runners, unchanged effort/search limits, all 106 completed route SVGs byte-identical, and no new completion or DRC failures. The five completed selected SRJ28 cases take 19.26% less total time (3.15% including the unchanged timeout); the heaviest completed case is 39.16% faster and reproduces a 37.01–44.80% speedup in a four-pass order control. Dataset01 is 2.92% faster in one paired run, while SRJ18 total time is effectively flat. These end-to-end figures measure the combined solver changes; they are not isolated attribution to this PR. Peak RSS is mixed and variable, including a 19.24% increase for sample 37 in the primary run that does not consistently reproduce in the order control. No uniform RSS reduction is claimed. Full per-case results, quality checks, memory quantiles, limitations and workflow links are in the consumer PR.

Snapshot regression coverage now records both optimizations with the original behavior as the live oracle:

- [Owned-metadata snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/3399475ae8c84d988bbf918311c433b8cfcf78f9/tests/__snapshots__/owned-regional-hop-metadata-cache.test.ts.snap): 1,447 → 82 hop-ID evaluations in the uninterrupted case, plus explicit queue-clear, best-cost-reset and neighbor-replacement cases. body:
`GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` introduces two different-net SMT-pad overlaps when given the captured Pipeline9 `sample006` input immediately after trace-width assignment. The input has no physical pad overlap; the output crosses `pcb_smtpad_6` and `pcb_smtpad_11` by approximately 0.0450793 mm.

body:

title: Preserve via-in-pad policy in regenerated TI samples
description: Preserves imported board via-in-pad permissions in the published TI routing samples, ensuring routers receive the source policy by updating the samples to include the allowViaInPad field and validating it against the Circuit JSON boards policy.
body:
**Motivation:** Preserve imported board via-in-pad permissions in the published TI routing samples so routers receive the source policy.

**Actual:** Samples 021–026 were generated with core `0.0.2165` and omit `allowViaInPad`, including four boards whose Circuit JSON explicitly permits vias in pads. The public declaration and validator also omit this policy.

**Expected / fix:** Pin released core `0.0.2188`, update its required props peer to `0.0.705`, and regenerate samples 021–026 from the SHA-256-verified Altium sources. Samples 021, 022, 024, and 025 now emit `true`; samples 023 and 026 emit `false` for an unspecified source policy. Add `allowViaInPad?: boolean` to the public declaration and generator template, and require each TI sample's policy to equal `pcb_board.is_via_in_pad_allowed ?? false` in the existing validator. The type remains optional for the older KiCad samples.

**Validation:**

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- `bun run generate:ti --source-root ../regen-ti-sources`
- `bun run test`: all 26 samples and 858 through-hole obstacles pass.
- All 18 negative checks reject missing, inverted, or string-valued policies across the six TI samples.
- TypeScript consumer checks and the actual declaration generator round trip pass.
- `bun run build`

Regeneration adds only the policy field to each SRJ; the Circuit JSON and comparison SVGs are byte-identical.

**Related:** Uses the released fix from [tscircuit/core#4689](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4689).

title: Reject jointly incompatible escape sites before native carrier search
description: This PR implements early rejection of incompatible native escape domains in the AM3352 hard-length surface routing, preventing unnecessary carrier negotiation on incompatible pair seeds.
body:
Native hard-length surface routing can spend its carrier-search budget on individually reachable escape sites that have no compatible joint assignment. In the AM3352 case, DDR_D13/D11/D9/DQM1 each have choices, but all 1,344 combinations conflict. This reuses bounded arc-consistency pruning on escape copper and full-stack drill compatibility before carrier negotiation. Proven-incompatible pair seeds return immediately; unsupported choices are removed. Exhausting the support-check budget keeps unproven choices and continues routing. The check is enabled for the hard-length native surface policy; the established unbounded legacy search remains intact. Manufacturing limits, supplied copper and final acceptance are unchanged. The regression fixture is derived entirely from the existing public full-DDR input, with geometry-derived native length limits and runtime-generated pair/CK repair geometry. No captured intermediate route dump or manual copper is added. Validation: two new integration tests pass (14 assertions); typecheck and diff checks pass. The negative control remains searching under the previous policy while the updated bounded policy rejects before 5,000 yields; a feasible four-signal control with generated DQS0 released still produces a candidate and preserves the other pairs/input. ## Benchmark effect **Complete: fresh Blacksmith base 11/11 and head 11/11; all checks green on the final production revision.** Same Linux x64 4-CPU / 16-GiB workspace, Bun 1.4.0, sequential base/head, JSC RAM setting 2 GiB and heap growth 1.05. Each policy receives the same cloned native state, options and 250,000-yield cap. title: Reproduce native AM3352 ordinary escape failures after pair planning
description: Reproduces failures in the native AM3352 surface search related to ordinary escape domains, adding tests for specific scenarios without altering existing routing behavior.
body:
The native AM3352 surface search can now select all three differential pairs, but the next stage rejects ordinary escape domains. Quiet, ambiguous or incomplete strobe observations remain unevaluated. Successful checks without characterization remain illustrative; finite simulation never claims DDR compliance. Existing probes/eyes and stimulus-clock folds remain supported. An independent raw-waveform audit checks crossings, capture times, AC acquisition, continuous DC validity and folded interpolation.

Pin the immutable prepared archive from [ibis-to-spice #1](https://github.com/tscircuit/ibis-to-spice/pull/1). Remove the sibling-mutating postinstall builder, declaration rewriting and its esbuild dependency. The converter needs no install-time build approval. Keep a stable executable entry for Bun Git installs. Default native tools to a shared cache outside project paths so spaces in the checkout do not break wxWidgets.

Browser inspection exposed an offline report bug: source-mode Function.toString() included a transpiler closure helper without its definition, disabling controls. Emit standalone browser JavaScript from the packaged typed source and add a regression check. Waveform and eye interaction were verified in Chrome. Canonicalize the TSX config path for macOS path aliases and keep temporary test projects outside the hashed source tree.

Validation: an archive of exact public HEAD `cd1e7db4384bdd599c29002a49aa91680659d449` passes both TypeScript checks and all 150 tests in parallel. Packaging commit `644d55f01d83379c0cac26bb3e63daf28447b770` additionally passed fresh-cache and warm frozen Bun 1.3.14 installs, fresh-store and warm frozen pnpm 11.25.0 installs, build, root/TSX APIs, both CLIs, converter parser/loader/conversion and byte-identical artifacts/locks. Pipeline consumers pass strict NodeNext with skipLibCheck enabled; converter declarations separately pass with it disabled. The board project with the final public pin passes its four tests, typecheck and all five builds.

The separate native routed-copper FastHenry repair remains outside this PR. These changes do not establish complete full-board extraction convergence or hardware DDR compliance.
